data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew name Yaaqov meaning 'he supplants' or 'he deceives' (Jacob). In the Old Testament, Jacob was a deceiver and supplanter, who God blessed despite his imperfections. In the New Testament, St. James the Just, also known as Jacob, was a leader of the Jerusalem church.

biblical_reference.note: Jacob was the third son of Isaac and Rebecca, and the older brother of Esau. He received the blessing of the firstborn from Isaac, which infuriated Esau, leading to years of conflict between the two.

saint_reference.note: Jacob of Sarug was a Syriac Christian bishop, theologian, and poet. He is best known for his hymns, which were influential in the development of the liturgical music of the Syriac Orthodox Church.

Jacob, the Old Testament patriarch, experienced many trials and challenges in his life, including deceiving his own father, Isaac, to secure the right to the blessings. Despite his past, Jacob became the father of the 12 tribes of Israel and was transformed into a man of faith.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Jacobo is a reminder of God's mercy and grace, as demonstrated through the life of Jacob in the Old Testament. This illustrates the idea that God sees our potential and our future, rather than just our past mistakes or current shortcomings.
